{{short description|American biostatistician}}
'''Marie Davidian''' is an American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] known for her work in [[Longitudinal study|longitudinal data analysis]] and [[precision medicine]]. She is the [[John Stuart Hunter|J. Stuart Hunter]] Distinguished Professor of Statistics at [[North Carolina State University]].{{r|named}} She was president of the [[American Statistical Association]] for 2013.{{r|elected|reminisce}}

==Education and career==
Davidian was born in [[Washington, D.C.]]{{r|sned1}} She did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Virginia]], initially in [[mechanical engineering]] but changing her major to [[applied mathematics]] after becoming fascinated by statistics in a class taught by David P. Harrington.{{r|reminisce}}

She completed her PhD in 1986 from the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], under the supervision of [[Raymond J. Carroll]], with a dissertation on ''Variance Function Estimation in Heteroscedastic Regression Models''.{{r|mgp}} 

She joined the North Carolina State faculty in 1987,{{r|named}}
and also holds an adjunct professorship at [[Duke University]].{{r|duke}}

==Books==
Davidian is the author of ''Nonlinear Models for Repeated Measurement Data'' (with D. M. Giltinan, CRC Press, 1995){{r|skovgaard}} and editor of ''Longitudinal Data Analysis'' (with Fitzmaurice, Verbeke, and Molenberghs, CRC Press 2008).{{r|robinson|roy}}

==Awards and honors==
Davidian is a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|reminisce}}

She is the 2007 winner of the Janet L. Norwood Award for Outstanding Achievement by a Woman in the Statistical Sciences,{{r|norwood}}
the 2009 winner of the [[Snedecor Award|George W. Snedecor Award]] "for fundamental contributions to the theory and methodology of longitudinal data, especially nonlinear mixed effects models; for significant contributions to the analysis of clinical trials and observational studies, and for leadership as president of ENAR, as editor, and as a member of the International Biometric Society council",{{r|sned1|sned2}}
and the 2011 winner of the [[Florence Nightingale David Award]] "for important contributions to the development of methods for analyzing data from longitudinal studies and clinical trials, and for outstanding leadership and dedication to the statistical profession".{{r|fnd}}

She was named Hunter Distinguished Professor in 2017,{{r|named}} after previously holding the William Neal Reynolds Professorship since 2005.{{r|reynolds}}

In 2018 Davidian was recipient of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award|American Statistical Association's Founders Award]].{{r|ASAFoundersAward}}
